content.title: Everyone Has Everything—Why Does My Life Feel So Incomplete?
content.subtitle: How social media’s artificial glamour and the trap of comparison rob us of contentment.
content.body:
Fingers keep scrolling endlessly through the social media newsfeed. Joyful photos of someone buying a new flat, dazzling reels of another person’s foreign tour, someone's fine dining at an expensive restaurant, or delightful moments of a happy married life.

While scrolling, a subconscious sigh builds up inside the chest. The heart then involuntarily asks—"They have moved so far ahead in life; they are so happy! What happened to mine? Why is there so much struggle, so much incompleteness in my destiny?"

Within moments, a sharp dissatisfaction and bitterness toward one's own settled home, work, and even simple yet peaceful life begin to take root. The very blessings we are immersed in all day suddenly feel trivial and dull before someone else’s flash of glamour.

Tears Behind the Screen vs. Smiles in Front of the Camera

We easily forget that on social media, people showcase only the brightest, filtered, and curated parts of their lives. No one puts their failures, late-night tears, broken relationships, family turmoil, or debt burdens in front of the camera.

We compare other people's edited best moments with the daily struggles and fatigue of our real lives. This unequal and meaningless comparison breeds toxic inferiority, envy, and severe ingratitude within our hearts. The mind then stops seeing the good and focuses solely on what is lacking.

The Timeless Solution from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ

Fourteen hundred years ago, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ showed us the most beautiful path to escape this deadly mental and spiritual disease of comparison. He said:

“Look at those who are beneath you in worldly matters and do not look at those who are above you, for it is more suitable that you do not underestimate the blessings of Allah.” (Sahih Muslim: 2963)

Today, social media forces us to do the exact opposite. Trapped by algorithms, we spend twenty-four hours looking only at those who possess more abundance. As a result, we overlook the thousands of infinite blessings right in front of our eyes and forget to be grateful to Allah.

In the Holy Quran, Allah, Glorious and Exalted is He, warns about this in profound words:

“And do not strain your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [various] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.” (Surah Ta-Ha: 131)

Ways to Soothe the Mind from This Toxic Comparison Trap:

1. Practice digital detox and have the courage to unfollow: Immediately unfollow or mute the pages, profiles, or influencers whose content triggers dissatisfaction and unnecessary sighs regarding your own life. No trend is more important than your mental and spiritual peace.

2. Count your unseen blessings: Take just five minutes daily to reflect on what Allah has gifted you that remains an elusive dream for millions—a healthy body, a roof over your head, guaranteed daily meals, and the simple yet priceless blessing of breathing safely.

3. Pray for barakah when seeing others' good fortune: Overcome inner narrowness upon seeing someone's success or joy and say—"Ma sha Allah, Allahumma barik lahu" (May Allah bless it). This keeps the heart free from malice, and the angels pray for the same goodness for you.

4. Remember, this world is not a permanent stage: Success will not be judged by how shiny someone’s timeline appears. On the scales of the Hereafter, the true assessment will rely on the gratitude, patience, and taqwa within our hearts toward our Lord.

The person who learns to be content with what they have is richer and more peaceful than all the billionaires in the world. This tranquility of the heart is a believer’s true wealth.
